descriptionChirho: Describing a person as sacred, devout, or set apart by God; used as adjective or substantive ('the Holy One') in reference to God, Christ, or godly persons. Distinguished from ἅγιος by emphasizing inherent moral purity and covenant faithfulness rather than ceremonial separation. Multilingual evidence: spa 'santo/Santo,' hin 'पवित्र' (pavitra, sacred/pure), arb 'قُدّوسَ/قُدّوسٌ' (quddūs, most holy — a divine attribute), kor '거룩하신–이여' (O Holy One, vocative), swa 'mtakatifu/Mtakatifu' (holy person). Covers Acts 2:27, 13:35, Titus 1:8, Hebrews 7:26, Revelation 15:4, 16:5.

Substantival neuter plural referring to sacred blessings, holy decrees, or covenant promises of God; specifically used in Acts 13:34 (τὰ ὅσια Δαυὶδ τὰ πιστά, 'the holy and sure blessings of David') alluding to Isaiah 55:3 LXX. This is a distinct lexicographic sense because the referent shifts from persons to abstract sacred realities. Multilingual evidence: spa 'santas' (fem. pl. sacred things), hin 'पवित्र–वस्तुएं' (pavitra vastuen, holy things/objects), arb 'قُدسِيّاتِ' (qudsiyyāt, sacred things — a distinct nominal form from قُدّوس), kor '거룩한–것들을' (holy things, accusative), swa 'matakatifu' (holy things, noun class 6 plural).
